text: Started on a folder that holds CSV and .xlsx files (also in subfolders), the home page lists every dataset found with its file name, sheet name for Excel, row count and column count.

GET /api/datasets/<id>/profile returns a JSON object mapping every column name to one of geospatial, temporal, categorical, numerical or other, and the same mapping is saved as a JSON file in the app's output folder.

Columns named lat, lon, lng, latitude or longitude (any case) are geospatial; date columns are temporal; integer and float columns are numerical; text columns with at most 50 distinct values and at most 50% distinct are categorical; other text columns are other.
A dataset with a temporal and a numerical column shows a time-series line chart of that numerical column over the temporal column on its dashboard page.
A dataset with a categorical and a numerical column shows a bar chart of the numerical column summed per category on its dashboard page.
A dataset with latitude and longitude columns shows a 3D map of its points, drawn as a Plotly 3D scatter, on its dashboard page; a dataset without them shows no map.
A dataset with no matching rule shows its column types and a table of its first rows and no charts, and the page loads without error.
Every dashboard page shows the dataset's column types and a table of its first 20 rows.
No page served by the app references a script, stylesheet, font or image on another host; every asset URL in the home and dashboard pages returns 200 from the app itself.
For a dataset with more rows than the map cap (default 50,000), the map data sent to the browser holds at most the cap and the page shows how many points are shown out of the total.
One launcher command, given a folder, starts the app on localhost and opens the dashboard home page in the default browser.
An empty or unreadable file in the folder is listed on the home page as could not be read, and the other datasets still list and open.
A Dockerfile and a Start-DataBoot.ps1 script are provided; the script checks Docker is running, mounts the chosen folder read-only, starts the container and opens the browser.
TSV, JSON, JSONL, GeoJSON and Parquet files in the folder are listed as datasets with their row and column counts, and a Parquet file gives the same column types and charts as the same data in CSV.

Files that are not a supported data type (for example .xls or .pdf) are listed in an Other files table on the home page with their type, size in bytes and modified date, without a link to a dashboard.

The charts API and dashboard page give a donut for a categorical column with 2 to 5 values (none for 6 or more), a histogram for a numerical column, a scatter and a correlation heatmap for two or more numerical columns, and a country map for a column of country names, with at most 8 charts per dataset.
Every chart on a dashboard page has exactly one rule caption and one count in the form 'N of M points' or 'N of M rows' (singular 'point' or 'row' when M is 1), and the page shows no other sentences.

Each dashboard offers XLSX and PPTX downloads; the XLSX opens in openpyxl with a first sheet named Data headed by the column names and at least one native chart, and the PPTX opens in python-pptx with a title slide plus one slide per chart, each holding a native chart.
The product is called DataBoot: the home page title and h1 read DataBoot, every dashboard title ends with ' - DataBoot', and no page says DataOS.
A .parquet file that cannot be read is listed on the home page as could not be read with its reason, and the other datasets still list and open.
Every count of 1,000 or more on the home and dashboard pages (rows, columns, bytes, N of M) is shown with thousands separators, for example 1,234 of 60,000.

On the home and dashboard pages each table's title (Datasets, Could not be read, Other files, Columns, First rows) is an h2 heading inside the table caption, and column headers show the column names in their original case.

requirements.txt lists xlsxwriter==3.3.0, python-pptx==1.0.2, openpyxl==3.1.5 and pyarrow==26.0.0, and the repository vendors none of these libraries; an XLSX exported by the app reopens in openpyxl without a 'no default style' warning.
On a dashboard page the Plotly tool bar of each chart is visible without hovering, and its buttons can be reached with the Tab key.

When one sheet of an Excel workbook cannot be read, the "Could not be read" table on the home page lists it as the file name and sheet (for example book.xlsx - Lookup), and the other sheets of that workbook still list and open as datasets.
A .json or .jsonl file that is not valid JSON is listed as could not be read with the note "invalid JSON"; valid JSON that is not a list of records keeps the note "not a list of records".
The country map lists countries sorted by value, largest first, like the bar chart; the 3D map titles its z axis and colour bar with the name of the z column.

Start-DataBoot.ps1 creates the venv with the newest Python from 3.11 to 3.13 it finds: it tries py -3.13, py -3.12 and py -3.11 in that order, then python only when that python reports a version from 3.11 to 3.13, so a machine with Python 3.12 and 3.14 and no 3.11 gets a 3.12 venv.

When no Python 3.11 to 3.13 is found, or venv creation or a pip install returns a non-zero exit code, Start-DataBoot.ps1 prints a message naming the failed step, deletes the partial .venv folder, waits for a key press so the window stays open, and exits with code 1 instead of running .venv\Scripts\python.exe.
A test fails if Start-DataBoot.ps1 creates the venv with one hardcoded Python version (for example only py -3.11) instead of trying 3.13, 3.12 and 3.11.

When one sheet's XML in an Excel workbook is corrupt (truncated or not XML), the other sheets of that workbook still list and open as datasets, and the corrupt sheet is listed under "Could not be read" with its sheet name (for example book.xlsx - Bad) and the note "not a valid xlsx".

GET /api/datasets/<id>/charts gives every chart a numeric score from 0 to 1 by its kind's fixed rule: line = |Spearman rho| of value vs time, bar and donut = Gini of the category totals drawn, scatter = |Pearson r|, histogram = min(1, |skew|/3), heatmap = largest off-diagonal |r|, 3D map and country map = 0.6; fewer than 2 values or constant values give 0. The scores match hand-computed values on fixture data to 2 decimals.

Charts in the charts API and on the dashboard page are ordered by score, highest first, with ties kept in the fixed chart order (3D map, country map, line, bar, donut, histogram, scatter, heatmap); loading the same dataset twice gives the same order and scores.
On the dashboard page the first chart spans the full content width and the other charts sit two per row at desktop width and one per row at phone width; the First rows table comes after every chart.

In the Explorer app each chart's rule caption ends with ' · score ' and the chart's score with 2 decimals (for example '· score 0.82'), and the score matches the charts API; captions in the Business, Map, Monitoring and Survey apps show no score (gate 181).

A KPI strip at the top of the dashboard shows rows, columns, % missing and the sum of each of the first 3 numerical columns, with thousands separators; with a filter active the figures are those of the filtered rows.

The dashboard shows one dropdown per categorical column and a from/to date range when a temporal column exists; choosing a value or range makes the charts API, called with the same query parameters, return smaller row counts (N of M) and KPI figures that match the filtered rows.

Filter state is kept in the page URL: opening a dashboard URL with filter query parameters shows the filtered charts and KPIs with the controls preset, the browser Back button returns to the previous filter state, each active filter shows as a removable chip that drops only that filter, and a 'Clear filters' button returns to the unfiltered view (gate 175).

Clicking a bar or a donut slice sets that category as the filter on its column: the URL, the dropdown and every chart and KPI update to the filtered rows; clicking the active bar again removes that filter, and a donut filter is removed with its chip or 'Clear filters' (gates 175, 178).

XLSX and PPTX exports opened with filter query parameters hold only the filtered rows (fewer Data sheet rows, smaller chart totals). The XLSX first sheet is still Data, and an XLSX sheet named Summary lists each active filter, or 'Filters: none' when there is none. The PPTX title slide lists the same filters and says 'Rows: N of M' (filtered of total) when filters are active and 'Rows: M' when not (gate 176).
On a 200,000-row CSV, a charts API request with a category filter returns in under 1 second in the test image.

On a 200,000-row CSV, the first request for the dashboard page or the charts API without filters (cold start, after the file read) answers in at most 5 seconds in the test image; column types are classified on the first 10,000 rows only, while charts and KPIs use all loaded rows (gate 176).

Detection by the ordered rule table: GET /api/datasets/<id>/app returns the app, the rule id and the list of apps the dataset qualifies for; a points fixture (lat, lon and at most 2 numerical columns) gives map/R1, a sales fixture (date, category, amount, no coordinates) gives business/R2, a fixture with only numerical columns gives explorer/R3, a fixture with lat/lon, 3 or more numerical columns and coordinates in fewer than 50% of rows does not give map, and repeated requests return the same answer.
Every dataset page shows a badge with the detected app and rule, for example 'App: Business (rule R2)' for the sales fixture and 'App: Explorer (rule R3)' for the numerical-only fixture.

A 'View as' switch lists exactly the apps the dataset qualifies for (Explorer always among them) and is absent when only Explorer qualifies; picking an app shows that app's layout and puts app=<name> in the URL, opening that URL shows the same app, and an app the dataset does not qualify for shows the detected app instead.

The Business app shows one KPI card per measure (up to 3 numerical columns: first those whose name contains amount, revenue, sales, total, price, value, cost, qty or quantity in any case, in column order, then the other numerical columns in column order; the first is the primary amount, gate 179) with the sum for the latest full period, an arrow icon plus signed percent with 1 decimal plus the text 'up', 'down' or 'no change' against the previous period, and a sparkline; on the sales fixture the values and percent match hand-computed ones, and with no previous value the card shows 'n/a' and no arrow.

The Business app shows a trend line of the primary amount summed per period at the automatic grain (day, week, month or year from the date span); with 2 or 3 measures it shows one trend chart per measure, each with a single y-axis.

The Business app shows a leaderboard of horizontal bars: the top 10 categories by primary amount, sorted descending, then one 'Other' bar holding the sum of the rest, each bar with its value printed on it with thousands separators.

The leaderboard groups by the first categorical column with no active filter in drill order (categorical columns sorted by distinct count ascending, ties by column order, gate 179); clicking a leaderboard bar regroups it by the next column in that order within the clicked category, updates the URL and shows a breadcrumb such as 'All › region: North'; clicking 'All' in the breadcrumb or pressing Back returns to the previous level, and bars at the last categorical level and the 'Other' bar do not drill.

The Business app shows a change table with the columns category, previous period, latest period and delta; each delta shows its sign, and its cell colour is grey for zero and two different hues for positive and negative deltas.

The Map app draws a 2D map of the points on the bundled world outline with a height between 65% and 75% of the viewport at desktop and phone width; points are coloured by the primary numeric (the AC-46 name rule, gate 179) on a one-hue sequential scale whose colour bar is titled with that column's name.

With more than 5,000 rows with coordinates the Map app draws hexagonal density cells, fewer marks than points, each cell's tooltip giving its point count, and the counts sum to the rows with coordinates; with 5,000 or fewer it draws one mark per point.

In the Map app, clicking a point shows that row's column values in a side panel that also holds a top-regions bar chart (gate 179: the country column if there is one, else the categorical column with the fewest distinct values, at least 2; ranked by the sum of the primary numeric, else by row count; top 10 then one 'Other' bar); a '3D view' button replaces the map with the Plotly 3D scatter and a second press brings the 2D map back.

In every app (Explorer, Business, Map, Monitoring, Survey) no Plotly figure has a yaxis2 or any second y-axis, every chart shows a tooltip on hover, and every chart has a 'view as table' toggle that shows a table of the chart's plotted values and switches back to the chart.

Every number of 1,000 or more on the Business and Map pages (KPI cards, value labels, change table, side panel, axis ticks and tooltips) is shown with thousands separators, for example 12,345, except values of identifier, temporal and year-like columns (AC-59).

With app=business or app=map the XLSX and PPTX exports carry the title 'Business overview' or 'Map overview' (PPTX title slide, XLSX Summary sheet); Business exports hold KPIs, trend, leaderboard and change table in that order, Map exports a native lon/lat scatter chart then top regions; the XLSX first sheet is still Data and Summary is last; Explorer exports are unchanged.

docs/DESIGN.md has a 'Global chart rules' section listing: magnitude as sorted bars from zero, change over time as a line, part-to-whole as stacked bar with donut only for 2-5 parts, one y-axis, fixed categorical palette order with at most 8 then 'Other', at most 3 colour series on scatter and maps, one-hue sequential and two-hue diverging scales with a grey midpoint, legend at 2 or more series and direct labels at 4 or fewer, tooltip and table toggle on every chart, thousands separators.
Opening the Business and Map apps in a browser, drilling down, switching 'View as' and toggling the 3D view and table views makes no request to any host other than the app itself.

Thousands separators follow the column role: on the dataset pages of every app (First rows table, Map side panel, tooltips and table views) a numerical amount 12345 shows as 12,345, while a year-like column (name contains year or yr, or whole numbers all 1900-2100) shows 2024 and an identifier column (for example order_id) shows 10045; the text '2,024' never appears for a year column (gate 183).

Counts use the singular for exactly 1 and the plural otherwise, in captions, tooltips and panels: '1 point', '2 points', '0 points', '1 of 1 row', '1 of 5 rows'; no page or tooltip shows '1 points' or '1 rows'.

In the Explorer app, hovering a clickable bar shows a pointer cursor, as on clickable Business leaderboard bars, and the docs/DESIGN.md Cross-filter (AC-39) text says Explorer bars carry the same click cursor.

Line charts in every app keep an automatic y-range (a Business trend whose values run from 14,000 to 16,000 has a y-axis lower bound above 0), while bar charts start their value axis at 0; docs/DESIGN.md Global chart rules says the zero baseline is for bars only.
Every PPTX export's title slide shows the title on its first line and the source file name (with the sheet name for Excel) on a second line in a smaller font size than the title.

GET /api/datasets/<id>/app walks the rules in the order R1 Map, R5 Survey, R2 Business, R4 Monitoring, R3 Explorer (gate 183): monitoring/R4 for a fixture with a date column, 1 or more numerical columns and no categorical column; survey/R5 for a fixture with 4 or more categorical columns making at least 60% of its columns and at most 2 numerical columns, where whole-number 1..5 or 1..7 columns count as categorical for R5 only and only when the file has no other numerical column named by the AC-46 amount rule; a survey fixture that also has a date column opens as survey/R5 with business in its qualifies list; the page badge reads 'App: Monitoring (rule R4)' or 'App: Survey (rule R5)', and every round 5 fixture keeps its app and rule.

The Monitoring app shows one tile per numerical column with the latest value, the min and max over the selected period, a sparkline, and the change against the previous period of the same length as an arrow icon plus signed percent with 1 decimal plus 'up', 'down' or 'no change'; values match hand-computed ones on the monitoring fixture, and with no previous period (or 'All') the tile shows 'n/a' and no arrow.

The Monitoring app has a period selector with 7 days, 30 days, 90 days and All; picking one puts period=<7|30|90|all> in the URL and limits the tiles and the main line to rows within that many days of the latest timestamp, and opening that URL shows the same period.

The Monitoring app's main line plots the primary numerical column over time with its 7-point trailing rolling mean as a second line on the same y-axis (gate 183); on a fixture with one planted outlier exactly that point is marked as a spike with a marker and the text label 'spike' (|z| > 3 against the 30 points before it), and a fixture without outliers shows no 'spike' label.

The Survey app shows one horizontal bar chart per non-Likert question (categorical column), bars sorted by count descending, top 10 then one 'Other' bar, laid out two charts per row at desktop width and one per row at phone width; the counts match hand-computed ones on the survey fixture; up to 2 numerical columns that are not identifiers (for example age) are shown as histograms in a 'Respondents' section (gate 183).

In the Survey app a Likert question (all values on one known scale: agree, satisfied, likely, frequency never..always, 1..5 or 1..7; gate 183) is drawn as a 100% stacked horizontal bar with its segments in scale order, the neutral middle segment grey and the two sides in two different hues; the segment shares sum to 100%.

The Survey app has a cross-tab with two dropdowns listing the questions; picking a row and a column question shows a heatmap whose cells give the count and the row percent with 1 decimal, the row percents of each row sum to 100, the pick is kept in the URL, and the counts match hand-computed ones.

With app=monitoring or app=survey the XLSX and PPTX exports carry the title 'Monitoring overview' or 'Survey overview' (PPTX title slide, XLSX Summary sheet) and hold native charts (Monitoring: the main line; Survey: one bar chart per question); the XLSX first sheet is still Data and Summary is last.

The Business app picks week grain (ISO weeks starting Monday) for a sales fixture spanning 61 to 182 days and year grain for one spanning more than 1,096 days, and the trend values and KPI card sums match hand-computed per-week and per-year sums.

For a dataset that qualifies only for Explorer, the XLSX Summary sheet has no app title line and the PPTX title slide's first line is 'Data overview' (gate 187), the XLSX has Data first and Summary last with at least one native chart, and the PPTX has a title slide plus one slide with a native chart per Explorer chart.

The home page shows one circular drop portal (equal width and height, fully rounded) that accepts dropped files, plus a 'Choose files' control that picks several files and a 'Choose folder' control that picks a folder; the h1 still reads DataBoot, and when the app was started on a folder the dataset, 'Could not be read' and 'Other files' tables still follow the portal.

Uploading one file, several files, or a folder with a subfolder through the home page sends them to the app's /upload; the scan then lists every uploaded dataset with the same file name (relative path kept, for example sub/sales.csv), row count, column count and app as when the app is started on a folder holding the same files.
Uploaded files are stored in a temp folder outside the project and any launcher folder; after the app stops, that temp folder no longer exists, and a folder given to the launcher is left unchanged.

An upload larger than the cap (2 GB by default; tests set a small cap) is refused with HTTP 413, and the page shows a message naming the 2 GB limit and the launcher's -Folder option for larger drives; none of that upload's files are kept or listed.

After an upload a scan screen shows one log line per dataset with its file name (and sheet), row count, role counts in the form T<n> N<n> C<n> G<n>, and '-> <APP> (rule <id>)' matching /api/datasets/<id>/app (for example '-> BUSINESS (rule R2)' for the sales fixture), one line per unreadable file with its note, and the line '0 bytes uploaded to the internet'; the lines appear one after another (about 0.35 s apart, all within 2.5 s), an 'Open workspace' link to the first dataset is visible from the start, and the workspace of the first dataset opens by itself after the last line (gate 189).

Every dataset page shows one tab per dataset with the current one marked (aria-current), an archetype caption in the form 'APP: BUSINESS · RULE R2 · T1 N2 C2 · 288 ROWS' (detected app and rule, role counts, total rows; gate 189), the 'App: <name> (rule <id>)' badge, the filter chips, and its tiles in a 12-column grid.

In the Business, Map, Monitoring, Survey and Explorer apps every chart, card group and table sits in the same tile component: a landmark region named by a heading inside the tile; the charts API answers and the figures' data are the same as before round 7.

Dragging a tile by its header onto another tile's place reorders the tiles; after a reload that dataset shows the new order, while another dataset keeps its default order; with focus on a tile's move handle, Alt+Arrow keys move the tile one place and an aria-live region announces the new position (gate 189).

Every tile has an expand control that opens it in a full-screen overlay (a modal dialog); Esc or a click on the backdrop closes it and focus returns to the expand control; clicking a bar inside the overlay applies that filter (URL, chip and N of M counts change) and the filtered tile is shown expanded again.

The pages use one dark theme whatever the OS colour preference: page background #050a12, accent colours cyan #4de1ff and amber #ffb454, labels in a monospace system font, no @font-face; body and label text have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against their background; charts keep one y-axis, sorted bars from zero and direction shown by icon or text, not colour alone.

Tiles enter one after another and every entrance animation has ended within 0.6 s of page load, and a glow on a tile follows the pointer; with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce nothing animates, and with prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce no element has a backdrop-filter.

Every clickable chart mark (Explorer bars and donut slices, Business leaderboard bars, Survey question bars, Map top-region bars) can be reached with the Tab key, shows a visible focus ring, and Enter or Space does the same as a click.

Opening the home page, uploading files, waiting for the scan, opening the workspace, dragging, expanding and closing a tile, toggling a table view and filtering inside the overlay makes no request to any host other than the app itself.

docs/DESIGN.md has a section for the round 7 theme and tiles that lists the colour tokens (#050a12, #4de1ff, #ffb454), the mono label font, the tile parts (header, drag handle, expand, table toggle), the 12-column grid and the motion rules (0.6 s entrance, reduced motion, reduced transparency).
